base_member_text: [L54,L180,L377-L392,L487-L490] (HIGH/vertical-section convention) swvegatt cumulatively adds each ah value as a layer thickness, while momeqveg treats each ah value as an absolute section height corrected by bed change, so the same vegetation profile has incompatible vertical interpretations.
audit_member_text: [L379,L489,L543-L544] (MED/inconsistent vertical-section semantics) swvegatt treats each ahveg value as a thickness by adding ahtold, while momeqveg treats it as an absolute section height and only stores ahtold afterward, producing inconsistent layer geometry for multi-section vegetation.

base_member_text: [L420-L473,L492-L527] (HIGH/uninitialized saved state) totT is initialized only when t equals dt exactly; otherwise the nonlinear branch tests an undefined saved value and may read the still-unallocated unl and etaw arrays.
audit_member_text: [L420,L459-L473,L493-L496] (HIGH/uninitialized persistent state) Saved totT is initialized only when floating-point par%dt exactly equals par%t; otherwise its first comparison is undefined and can lead to use of unallocated unl/etaw arrays.

base_member_text: [L436-L440,L579-L619,L798-L810] (MED/saved-workspace shape) Saved vegetation work arrays are allocated only on their first call and never checked against later grid dimensions.
audit_member_text: [L421-L424,L436-L440,L604-L619,L798-L810] (LOW/state/dimension lifecycle) Several saved allocatable work arrays are allocated only once and never resized, so reuse with a changed grid shape retains incompatible bounds.

base_member_text: [L502-L510,L534-L556] (HIGH/stale section force) The above-wave-crest branch zeros the mean and nonlinear forces but not FvgCau/FvgCav, so enabling vegcanflo can reuse a canopy force from the previous section or cell.
audit_member_text: [L502-L557] (HIGH/stale per-layer state) When a vegetation section lies wholly above the wave crest, FvgCau and FvgCav are not reset, yet vegcanflo can still add their values from a preceding section or cell.

base_member_text: [L525-L536] (HIGH/dry-depth division) Nonlinear and in-canopy force terms divide by raw hh for every vegetated cell without a wet or positive-depth guard.
audit_member_text: [L525-L536] (HIGH/dry-cell division) Nonlinear and canopy-wave forces divide by s%hh for every vegetated cell without a wet-cell guard, so dry vegetated points can generate division-by-zero or NaN values.

base_member_text: [L109-L113] (LOW/file-error handling) The species-list read records iostat but never checks it before the names are used as filenames.
audit_member_text: [L103-L112] (MED/input error handling) Species-name reads record iostat in ier but never inspect it, so a short or malformed species list can leave names undefined and fail later in a misleading way.

base_member_text: [L621-L641] (HIGH/whole-array dry-depth division) swvegnonlin divides whole-domain arrays by hh and hh**3 before any wet-cell restriction, including in its Ursell-number and lookup-coordinate calculations.
audit_member_text: [L621-L622,L637-L641,L648-L680] (HIGH/dry-cell invalid arithmetic) swvegnonlin divides by s%hh and takes sqrt(g/s%hh) over the entire grid with no wet mask, making zero-depth cells feed infinities/NaNs into table interpolation and output profiles.

base_member_text: [L135-L154,L223-L239] (HIGH/unchecked map index) Positive vegetation-map values are used directly as veg(ind) subscripts without checking ind<=nveg, so an out-of-range species code causes invalid access.
audit_member_text: [L138-L153,L223-L239] (HIGH/unchecked input index) Spatial vegtype values are never checked against 0..par%nveg before being used as veg(ind), so an oversized map value causes out-of-bounds species access.

base_member_text: [L730-L769] (MED/unchecked singular denominator) bulkdragcoeff divides by sigm, sinh(k*hh), bveg, and alfav**0.76 without local guards, despite being callable with bed-adjusted plant height and shallow wave state.
audit_member_text: [L731-L769] (MED/unchecked physical denominator) bulkdragcoeff divides by sigm, hh, sinh(k*hh), bveg, and alfav powers without guarding calm, dry, zero-height, or zero-width cases.

base_member_text: [L135-L154] (MED/unsupported-option handling) The gridform select has no default branch, leaving vegtype uninitialized if an unsupported grid form reaches this routine.
[L93-L128,L174-L221,L262-L301] (MED/lifecycle/allocation) veggie_init allocates all vegetation state without an existing-allocation or grid-shape guard, so repeated initialization is unsafe.

[L180-L185,L325-L330] (LOW/unreachable option) The automatic bulk-drag path requires Cdveg<0, but initialization constrains every input Cd to the nonnegative range, making that documented path unreachable through this reader.

[L370-L399] (HIGH/dry-cell/singular wave calculation) Short-wave vegetation dissipation is evaluated without a wet mask and divides by sigm, while its hyperbolic terms use raw hh, allowing dry or zero-frequency cells to generate invalid values.

[L527,L686-L699] (MED/periodic integration) trapz integrates only 49 intervals for the 50-point periodic profile while the caller supplies Trep/50 spacing, omitting the closing interval from the last sample back to the first.

[L868-L882] (MED/partial output assignment) porcanflow overwrites vegetation forces only on interior staggered-loop bounds, leaving the remaining boundary entries dependent on initialization or prior calls.

audit_member_text: [L863-L865] (LOW/stale force state) porcanflow deliberately leaves Fcanu/Fcanv unchanged in non-canopy cells, so any runtime change from canopy to non-canopy would retain the prior canopy force.
